_comment: The authoritative Compose runtime contract (issue #167, EPIC B #81 Phase 6).
Before this file the canonical compose definition was documentation-shaped:
its security posture was asserted in a comment, its field set was whatever
had accumulated, and an adapter agreeing with it was a matter of review. This
file is the contract-shaped version. It names every field the canonical
runtime definition must declare, and every host privilege the deployment must
not need, and distribution/compose's test suite fails the build when either
Two lists, deliberately asymmetric. `fields` is checked against the CANONICAL
definition only, because that is the artifact adapters derive from; holding a
derived artifact to the full field set would make it a second definition
rather than a derivation. `prohibited` is checked against the canonical
definition AND every derived artifact, because a prohibition an adapter can
opt out of is not a prohibition.
Roles, not service names. A service is the engine or the web UI because of
the command it runs, never because of what it is called: apps/truenas calls
them backup-manager/backup-manager-ui and the canonical file calls them
rclone-manager/web-ui, and a check keyed on the name would silently stop
checking the moment someone renamed one.
_derived_comment: Every artifact derived from the canonical definition. distribution/compose's
completeness guard fails when a compose file exists under apps/*/compose or
apps/*/catalog that is not listed here, so a new adapter cannot arrive

fields.why: one canonical image, named identically by every service, so `command` is the only thing that varies between them.

the contract standardises 'command and runtime profile' as one field. A deployment that does not name its profile is a deployment whose host-dependent behaviour is implicit, which is the thing #167 exists to remove.
the HTTP listen port, published by exactly one service. The engine deliberately declares none, which is why this field is required of the web UI role only.

declared in the runtime definition rather than inherited from an image instruction and described in a comment. An operator reading this file has to be able to see what healthy means without reading the Dockerfile.

the start gate has to be a liveness question, not a backup-freshness one. web-ui declares depends_on: rclone-manager: service_healthy, so whatever the engine's healthcheck asks is what stands between an operator and the only LAN-facing listener. `backup-manager status` exits non-zero on any DEGRADED, STALE or FAILING set and on an instance with no configuration at all, so gating on it means a stale backup set, or a fresh install, keeps the UI from starting. /health/live needs no configuration and is deliberately outside /api/v1. Backup freshness stays the operator and alerting surface it was built to be.

the declared grace period the runtime shuts down inside. Without it the value is Docker's own 10s default, which is a default rather than a contract, and nothing anywhere records what the application actually needs.
survive a crash and a NAS reboot, stay down when an operator stopped it on purpose.
explicit UID/GID rather than the image's build-time default, because the state directory's ownership is the host's business and not the image's.
a read-only root filesystem is what makes the writable paths explicit rather than implied.
retention is evaluated in a timezone. Leaving it to the image's UTC default means the calendar boundaries an operator reasons about and the ones the engine applies are silently different.
the private application state: the lifecycle journal and the local-auth record. Separate from backup data, always.
the backup destination. Never the same mount as private state, and never a parent of it.

configuration comes from the host, never baked into the image, and the mount is a WRITABLE DIRECTORY the application owns rather than a read-only single file (issue #196). config.yaml lives inside it. The read-only single-file shape made three merged write paths inert inside a packaged container: every one of them replaces config.yaml through a temp file created in its own directory, which on that shape is the image's read-only rootfs. A directory can also be empty, which is how an app-store install honestly represents "not configured yet"; a bind mount cannot express that for a file, because Docker creates a directory at a missing source path.
credential material is a read-only file mount and nothing else. No credential belongs in this file or in the environment.
documented resource expectations, in the runtime definition rather than in prose that drifts from it.
the architectures this release claims. A deployment definition that does not say which architectures its image exists for cannot be checked against the release metadata.
how an operator pins a release. A tag is mutable; the contract has to say what the immutable reference is and where it is recorded.
the version of this contract the definition was written against, so a contract change is a visible edit rather than a silent divergence.
the profiles this runtime definition supports selecting, so `--profile=` above has a declared range rather than an open one.

_prohibited_comment: EPIC B #81 and issue #167's prohibition list. An absent setting and an
unnecessary setting are different claims, so these rules are only half the
evidence. The other half is a deployment that does real work without any of
them, and that already exists: apps/generic/tests/dockercli runs the real
built image with none of these settings, reaches health, and completes real
work. The static rules here prove the settings are absent; that suite proves
Each rule below has its own positive control in contract_test.go: the real
definition is mutated to require the setting, and the rule has to fire AND
name the service and the value. Three preflight rules in this repository have
already failed open, so a rule nobody has watched fail is a comment.

prohibited.why: privileged mode disables the container boundary entirely.
host networking puts the engine on every host interface, which is exactly the isolation the two-service topology exists to provide.
the host PID namespace lets the container see and signal host processes.
the host IPC namespace is shared memory with the host.
the Docker socket is root on the host with extra steps.
mounting a host system directory is unbounded host filesystem access; every path this runtime needs is a named mount.
least-privilege capabilities. Nothing this runtime does needs a capability a plain non-root process does not already have.
turning off the host's own confinement is the same class of exception as privileged mode.
